title: Forecast Calculations Adventure
welcome_lead: Now you'll calculate multi-month closing balances and fix a cash-flow problem.

walkthroughs.body_html:
A forecast's closing balance becomes next month's opening balance.

So a bad month doesn't just hurt itself — it drags the next month down too.

If outflows > inflows, the net cash flow is negative.

If the running closing balance dips below zero, you have a cash gap — and need a remedy fast.

Speed up inflows: chase debtors, ask for deposits, sell off slow stock.

Slow down outflows: negotiate longer credit from creditors, delay non-urgent spending, use an overdraft.

mcqs.q: Why are cash flow and profit different on different time-scales?
options: Porter's Five Forces are five physical security measures for a factory.
Cash flow only matters at year-end.

Profit is recognised when a sale is made (even on credit); cash flow is when money actually moves. A profitable sale today may produce no cash for 60 days while bills are due — creating a cash-flow problem despite profit.
Cash flow and profit are the same thing measured differently.

mcqs.q: Why can a profitable business still fail?
options: Cash flow only matters at year-end.
Because cash flow and profit are different — a business may be profitable on paper but run out of cash to pay bills, especially if customers owe money or stock ties up funds.
If a business is profitable it cannot run out of money.
Profitable businesses fail only when employees steal.
Profitable businesses fail only when employees steal.
Porter's Five Forces are five business strategies a firm should choose between.
Porter's Five Forces are five physical security measures for a factory.

Competitive rivalry, threat of new entrants, threat of substitutes, bargaining power of suppliers, bargaining power of buyers — together determining industry attractiveness and potential profitability.
